cultures.name: Caldric
cultures.art_description: Rooted stances that draw strength from the ground. Masters set their feet and a spear-thrust carries the weight of a hillside; the old ones could wake runestones by touch.

festivals.name: Kindling Night
festivals.description: Every hearth is put out and relit from the runestone brazier; children carry the new flame home.

festivals.name: Stonewake
festivals.description: Villagers walk the runestone circle, scrub the stones and renew the carved wards.

festivals.name: Last Sheaf
festivals.description: Harvest feast; the final sheaf is braided into a figure and kept above the door.

cultures.name: Seirune
cultures.art_description: Flowing footwork and redirected force: a strike is received, turned and returned. Lantern-school adepts add Stormstitch, a sudden flash-step borrowed from lightning.

festivals.name: Thousand Lanterns
festivals.description: Paper lanterns are set adrift on the tide to guide the drowned home.

festivals.name: Blade Oath Day
festivals.description: Young retainers swear to their house before the family sword.

festivals.name: First Storm
festivals.description: Crowds gather on the sea walls to greet the first great storm; Stormstitch duels are held in the rain.

cultures.greeting: A shallow bow, palms flat at the sides: "The tide returns."

cultures.name: Ongur
cultures.art_description: Breath-driven movement: riders who can stand in the saddle at full gallop, arrows that curve on a gust, leaps that hang in the air a heartbeat too long.

festivals.name: Games of the Three Winds
festivals.description: Wrestling, horse racing and archery; winners are named in songs across the steppe.

festivals.name: White Month
festivals.description: New year: debts forgiven, elders visited, the first milk scattered to the sky.

cultures.greeting: Both hands offered, palms up: "Is your horse strong?" (answer: "As the wind.")

cultures.name: Solenne
cultures.art_description: Fire drawn from the breath and shaped by chant and stance. Temple adepts hold the Dawnflame, a white fire that burns corruption and soothes the faithful.

festivals.name: Dawnrise
festivals.description: The whole city keeps vigil through the night and greets the equinox sunrise with ten thousand candles.

festivals.name: Feast of Embers
festivals.description: Relics are carried through the streets; the sick are brought to the Dawnflame braziers.

cultures.greeting: Hand over heart: "Dawn upon you." (answer: "And never dusk.")

cultures.name: Urrokai
cultures.art_description: The orc war-art: breath, heartbeat and shout become one. A Bloodroar stance can shrug off wounds for a few moments; masters shake stone with a war-cry.
values: strength proven in front of the clan
no debt left unpaid, good or ill

festivals.name: The Tusking
festivals.description: Youths who have killed their first boar are given their clan scar.

festivals.name: Red Moon Moot
festivals.description: Clans meet under the red moon to settle feuds by challenge and to choose war or peace.

cultures.greeting: Forearm clasp, foreheads touch: "Strong blood." (answer: "Stronger clan.")

cultures.name: Shenlu
cultures.art_description: Cultivated qi, called 'inner current' in the peaks, is refined through realms and released through sword, palm and step. Sect masters are said to ride lightning between summits.

festivals.name: Ascending Peaks Tournament
festivals.description: Every sect sends its best young disciples to duel on the Nine Stairs; rankings decide a decade of prestige.

festivals.name: Lantern of Returning Souls
festivals.description: Families burn paper offerings at ancestral shrines.

cultures.greeting: Fist in palm, a short bow: "May your path ascend."

cultures.name: Veyl
cultures.art_description: Song and dance that speak to growing things: vines that bind, bark that hardens over skin, arrows whose shafts sprout thorns. Also the root of the beast-bonding arts.

festivals.name: Night of Falling Light
festivals.description: Once a decade the Veyl gather in silence to watch the star shower that gave them their eyes.

festivals.name: Leafturn
festivals.description: Songs for every tree that died this year; saplings are planted in their place.

cultures.greeting: Palm raised, fingers spread like leaves: "Root and bough."

cultures.name: Durrow
cultures.art_description: Hammer-rhythm fighting: every blow timed to a heartbeat, heat stored in the body and released through iron. Masters' hammers glow orange mid-fight.

festivals.name: Founding Fire
festivals.description: The great forge is relit; every smith strikes one blow on a communal blade.

festivals.name: Book of Grudges Reading
festivals.description: Old grievances are read aloud; settled ones are struck through with ceremony.

cultures.greeting: A knock of knuckles on the chest, twice: "Stone and fire."
